Chapter 10: The Lasting Impact—Living with Change, Not Against It.
Picture this—the evening’s winding down, but nobody really wants to leave. The room’s filled with that special kind of warmth you get after sharing an honest conversation. The story of the maze and the cheese? It’s become more than just something they talked about. It’s now a lens for seeing the world a little differently.
They’ve realized something big: change isn’t the enemy. In fact, it’s always around, whether we like it or not. Sure, it shows up uninvited sometimes—maybe when we’re least prepared—but it always brings a chance to learn, and even to grow. That old fear of the unknown? It doesn’t seem quite so scary anymore. Instead, there’s this quiet confidence, a kind of inner calm. It’s the understanding that, whatever comes their way, they’ll figure it out.
One friend, thinking back on a year full of ups and downs, suddenly sees how those tough moments were actually the ones that changed her the most. Another, who’d always hated change, starts to feel curious—almost excited—about what might be waiting just around the corner.
When they finally say their goodbyes, it’s with a real sense of gratitude. Gratitude for the story, for each other, and for the gentle reminder that we’re all walking through our own maze. There’ll be obstacles, sure. Setbacks, disappointments—they’re part of the deal. But now, they know they’ve got what it takes to keep moving forward.
And the story? It sticks with them. It’s like a quiet nudge, reminding each of them to embrace change, to let go of what’s no longer helping, and to trust that somewhere, new cheese is just waiting to be found.
